A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Thoughtology study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison; relocated and relabeled appendix material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments and analyses of reasoning, context handling, safety, language, psycholinguistic stimuli, ASCII generation and budget-aware training, with supporting appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative rumination analyses, expanded CHASE evaluations and experiments on Qwen3 and gpt-oss.

M1.justification: The four-stage reasoning taxonomy and Section 11.2 GRPO training procedure, including MaxLength and MaxDiff rewards, are retained. Additional model evaluations and analysis metrics do not change the proposed training method.

E1.justification: The dataset and task coverage is retained. Section 12 reuses MATH-500 and AIME-24 for additional models; CHASE expands samples and splits within the existing question-answering and repository-level coding tasks.

E2.justification: Section 12 introduces Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 and gpt-oss-120b as direct comparison models for reasoning structure and length–accuracy analyses previously focused on DeepSeek-R1. This substantially expands the comparator scope of these central analyses; existing CHASE, safety and budget-training comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes CHASE-QA evaluation from 200 sampled examples to all 671, and CHASE-Code from 100 algorithms-split examples to all 500. Sections 3 and 9 replace character/word lengths with token lengths. v3 also introduces repetition/diversity metrics and additional model configurations, while Figure 8.2 drops response-generation time.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative rumination analyses across tasks, mathematical difficulty, correct versus incorrect answers, and psycholinguistic stimulus/control conditions (Figures 3.3b, 3.6, 4.4 and 9.3). Section 12 and Appendix B additionally examine generalization of reasoning patterns and length effects to two other LRMs.

E5.justification: The five-run psycholinguistic design, bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals and Spearman significance reporting are retained. Changed intervals and p-values accompany token-based measurement; no changed run-count, seed or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Under expanded test sets, Table 2 replaces Gemini-1.5-Pro/R1/V3 scores of 58/36/15 with 63.2/45.2/33.8 for CHASE-QA, and 42/38/22 with 38.2/36.6/36.6 for CHASE-Code. v3 adds rumination and cross-model findings, revises length-dependent statistics using tokens, and removes Figure 8.2's latency results. These are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 introduces explicit definitions for quantitative rumination measures and normalized lexical entropy in Equation (1). The budget-reward mathematics remains unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and seven principal DeepSeek-R1 findings are retained. The introduction and Section 12 extend the conclusions: Qwen3 shares R1-like reasoning stages, gpt-oss differs structurally, and both exhibit a reasoning-length sweet spot.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 revises the coding interpretation from R1 outperforming V3 to comparable performance. New discussion connects rumination with difficulty and accuracy, proposes differences between logical mathematical reasoning and probabilistic syntactic processing, and qualifies which patterns generalize across LRMs. Existing limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-wide code and model-output release statement with a repository address in Section 1, while removing Section 11.2's specific nano-aha-moment implementation-reference link. Existing API settings, prompts and budget-training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Qwen3 and gpt-oss reports and references supporting the new syntactic-versus-mathematical processing discussion, including Levy, Traxler and Mahowald et al. The broader background and research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained, with localized wording and heading edits. v3 removes the contents pages, inserts the other-LRM section before Discussion, and moves Author Contributions from Appendix A to the main document.

P2.justification: v3 adds multiple rumination and cross-model plots, redraws length plots with token axes, and removes Figure 8.2's latency panel. Table 6 gains an Overall column redisplaying values already in Table 7. The TMLR layout also substantially reflows figures, captions, tables and appendix examples.

improvement.justification: Quantitative rumination measurements and comparisons with two additional LRMs substantially strengthen evidence for central reasoning-behavior conclusions, addressing v2's largely qualitative rumination account and limited cross-model evidence. Full CHASE evaluations reduce dependence on small subsets and support a revised coding interpretation. Reproducibility information also improves. The added analyses remain exploratory, and Figure 8.2 loses latency evidence, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
